 Bail Appl. No.5289 of 2025  ------------------------------------
 Dated this the 10th day of June, 2025  ORDER
This bail application is filed under section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS').
2. Petitioner is the accused in Crime No.159 of 2025 of Thenmala Police Station registered for the offences punishable under sections 420, 406 and r/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

3. According to the prosecution, the accused who had taken loan from the de facto complainant for the purpose of construction of a cold storage and procuring dry fruits had, after repayment of a portion of the amount, failed to pay Rs.9.81 Crores and later removed the machineries that were installed in the cold storage and acted in violation of the agreement executed between them and thereby committed the offences alleged.

4. I have heard Sri.K.K.Dheerendrakrishnan, the learned counsel for the petitioner as well as Smt.
Sreeja V, the learned Public Prosecutor.
5. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner has been falsely arrayed as an accused and that he has no 2025:KER:41198 involvement in the alleged crime.
6. The learned Public Prosecutor opposed the bail application and submitted that custodial interrogation is necessary.
7. Petitioner is alleged to have failed to repay the loan availed from the de facto complainant mere failure to repay the loan cannot amount to a criminal offence.
However, the allegations indicate that the petitioner removed machineries that were hypothecated with the de facto complainant.

Though the said allegation can attract some of the offences alleged, I am of the view that custodial interrogation of the petitioner is not necessary, provided the petitioner subjects himself to interrogation.

Accordingly, this application is allowed on the following conditions:
(a) Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer on 19.06.2025 and shall subject himself to interrogation.
(b) If after interrogation, the Investigating Officer proposes to arrest the petitioner, then, he shall be released on bail on him executing a bond for Rs.50,000/- (Rupees fifty thousand only) with two Shanavas.A.M vs State Of Kerala on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147896972/
2 solvent sureties each for the like sum before the Investigating Officer.
(c) Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer as and when required and shall also co-operate with the investigation.
(d) Petitioner shall not intimidate or attempt to influence the witnesses; nor shall he tamper with the evidence.
(e) Petitioner shall not commit any similar offences while he is on bail.
(f) Petitioner shall not leave India without the permission of the 2025:KER:41198 Court having jurisdiction.

In case of violation of any of the above conditions or if any modification or deletion of the conditions are required, the jurisdictional Court shall be empowered to consider such applications, if any, and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law, notwithstanding the bail having been granted by this Court.

Sd/-
